title.zh: 卷一百三十六 列傳第二十四 陶安 詹同 朱升 崔亮 陶凱 曾魯 任昂 李原名 樂韶鳳
title.en: Volume 136 Biographies 24: Tao An, Zhan Tong, Zhu Sheng, Cui Liang, Tao Kai, Ceng Lu, Ren Ang, Li Yuanming, Le Shaofeng
title.raw: 卷一百三十六 列傳第二十四 陶安 詹同 朱升 崔亮 陶凱 曾魯 任昂 李原名 樂韶鳳 Volume 136 Biographies 24: Tao An, Zhan Tong, Zhu Sheng, Cui Liang, Tao Kai, Ceng Lu, Ren Ang, Li Yuanming, Le Shaofeng

sentences.zh: 陶安，字主敬，當塗人。

translations.literal: Tao An, with the style name Zhujing, was a man of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao An, styled Zhujing, was from Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 少敏悟，博涉經史，尤長於《易》。

translations.literal: In youth he was perceptive and quick; he ranged broadly through the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was exceptionally quick-witted; he read widely in the classics and histories and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 元至正初，舉江浙鄉試，授明道書院山長，避亂家居。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan Zhizheng era, he passed the Jiang-Zhe provincial examination, was appointed headmaster of the Mingdao Academy, and stayed at home to avoid the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhizheng reign, he passed the Jiang and Zhe regional examination and was appointed director of the Mingdao Academy; he then retired at home to escape the civil unrest.

sentences.zh: 太祖取太平，安與耆儒李習率父老出迎。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Taiping, An together with the venerable scholar Li Xi led the elders to go out and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor captured Taiping, An and the elder scholar Li Xi led the local elders out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 太祖召與語。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor summoned him and conversed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 安進曰：「海內鼎沸，豪傑並爭，然其意在子女玉帛，非有撥亂、救民、安天下心。

translations.literal: An advanced and said: "Within the seas the tripod boils; heroes struggle with one another, yet their intent lies in children, women, jade, and silks—they lack the mind to put chaos in order, save the people, and settle all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An spoke up: "The empire is in uproar and rival strongmen fight one another, but their aim is spoil and luxury, not to restore order, relieve the people, or bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 明公渡江，神武不殺，人心悅服，應天順人。

translations.literal: My lord has crossed the Yangzi: divine in martial prowess and sparing in killing; hearts rejoice and submit—he responds to Heaven and accords with men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace has crossed the Yangzi with a martial spirit that shuns needless slaughter; the people gladly submit. You answer Heaven's mandate and win men over.

sentences.zh: 以行吊伐，天下不足平也。」

translations.literal: By acting as one who comforts the wronged and punishes the guilty, all under Heaven is not enough to remain un pacified."
translations.idiomatic: March forth as the champion of the wronged, and pacifying the realm will be a small matter.

sentences.zh: 太祖問曰：「吾欲取金陵，何如？」

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor asked: "I wish to take Jinling—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "I mean to take Jinling. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「金陵，古帝王都。

translations.literal: An said: "Jinling is the ancient capital of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: An replied, "Jinling was the seat of emperors in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 取而有之，撫形勝以臨四方，何向不克？」

translations.literal: Take it and possess it; soothe its commanding terrain to look down on the four directions—what direction would not be overcome?"
translations.idiomatic: Seize it and hold its strategic heights to command the four quarters—what enemy could withstand you?"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 留參幕府，授左司員外郎，以習為太平知府。

translations.literal: He was kept to participate in the staff headquarters and appointed Left Department Assistant Director; Li Xi was made Taiping prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was retained on the military staff as Left Department Assistant Director, and Li Xi was appointed prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 習字伯羽，年八十余矣，卒於官。

translations.literal: Xi, style name Boyu, was more than eighty years old and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, styled Boyu, was over eighty and died in his post.

sentences.zh: 安從克集慶，進郎中。

translations.literal: An followed in the conquest of Jiqing and was promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: An accompanied the campaign that took Jiqing and was promoted to Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及聘劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至，太祖問安：「四人者何如？」

translations.literal: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were invited and arrived, the Taizu emperor asked An: "How are these four men?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were brought in, the emperor asked An, "What do you make of these four?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣謀略不如基，學問不如濂，治民之才不如溢、琛。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In strategy and planning your subject is not equal to Ji; in learning not equal to Lian; in talent to govern the people not equal to Yi and Chen."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your servant is no match for Ji in strategy, for Lian in scholarship, or for Yi and Chen in governing the people."

sentences.zh: 太祖多其能讓。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor greatly valued his ability to yield.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his modesty.

sentences.zh: 黃州初下，思得重臣鎮之，無逾安者，遂命知黃州。

translations.literal: When Huangzhou was first taken, he thought to obtain a weighty minister to guard it; none surpassed An, so he was ordered to govern Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangzhou was newly pacified, the emperor sought a senior official to secure it and found no one better than An, so he appointed him Huangzhou magistrate.

sentences.zh: 寬租省徭，民以樂業。

translations.literal: He eased rents and reduced corvée labor; the people thereby took joy in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced rents and levies, and the people settled contentedly into their work.

sentences.zh: 坐事謫知桐城，移知饒州。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to govern Tongcheng, then transferred to govern Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a disciplinary offense he was demoted to Tongcheng and later transferred to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 陳友定兵攻城，安召吏民諭以順逆，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Chen Youding's troops attacked the city; An summoned officials and people and instructed them on obedience and rebellion; they closed the city and firmly defended.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youding's army besieged the city, An rallied officials and commoners, explained the difference between loyalty and rebellion, and held the walls in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 援兵至，敗去。

translations.literal: Relief troops arrived and Chen's forces were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When relief arrived, the besiegers were defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲盡戮民之從寇者，安不可。

translations.literal: The various generals wished to slaughter all among the people who had followed the bandit; An would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to execute every civilian who had sided with the enemy, but An refused.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜詩褒美，州民建生祠事之。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor bestowed a poem in praise; the people of the prefecture built a living shrine to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him a poem of commendation, and the people of the prefecture raised a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，初置翰林院，首召安為學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu, the Hanlin Academy was first established and An was the first summoned as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Wu year the Hanlin Academy was founded, and An was the first scholar appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 時征諸儒議禮，命安為總裁官。

translations.literal: At the time various Confucians were summoned to discuss ritual; An was ordered to be chief editor.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars were summoned to debate ritual propriety, and An was made chief coordinator of the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 尋與李善長、劉基、周禎、滕毅、錢用壬等刪定律令。

translations.literal: Soon together with Li Shanchang, Liu Ji, Zhou Zhen, Teng Yi, Qian Yongren, and others he revised and determined codes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Li Shanchang, Liu Ji, Zhou Zhen, Teng Yi, Qian Yongren, and others in drafting the statutes.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，命知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year one he was ordered to draft imperial proclamations and concurrently edit the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongwu year he was charged with drafting edicts and compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗御東閣，與安及章溢等論前代興亡本末。

translations.literal: The emperor once took the eastern pavilion and with An and Zhang Yi and others discussed the roots and ends of the rise and fall of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held court in the Eastern Lodge and debated with An, Zhang Yi, and others the causes of rise and fall in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 安言喪亂之源，由於驕侈。

translations.literal: An said the source of ruin and disorder lies in arrogance and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: An argued that the root of dynastic collapse was arrogance and lavish excess.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「居高位者易驕，處佚樂者易侈。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Those who dwell in high position easily become arrogant; those who dwell in ease and pleasure easily become extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Those who hold high rank easily grow arrogant, and those who live in comfort easily grow extravagant.

sentences.zh: 驕則善言不入，而過不聞；

translations.literal: When arrogant, good words do not enter and faults are not heard;
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance shuts out good counsel so that faults go unheard;

sentences.zh: 侈則善道不立，而行不顧。

translations.literal: when extravagant, the good Way is not established and conduct is not looked back upon.
translations.idiomatic: extravagance uproots the right path so that conduct is no longer restrained.

sentences.zh: 如此者，未有不亡。

translations.literal: Those like this—none have failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who fall into this have never failed to fall.

sentences.zh: 卿言甚當。」

translations.literal: Your words are very apposite."
translations.idiomatic: Your analysis is entirely apt.

sentences.zh: 又論學術。

translations.literal: They again discussed learning and doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The conversation turned to learning and doctrine.

sentences.zh: 安曰：「道不明，邪說害之也。」

translations.literal: An said: "When the Way is not clear, heterodox doctrines harm it.
translations.idiomatic: An said, "When the Way is unclear, heretical teachings are to blame.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「邪說害道，猶美味之悅口，美色之眩目。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Heterodox doctrines harming the Way are like delicacies pleasing the mouth and beautiful colors dazing the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Heresy harms the Way as dainties please the palate and bright colors dazzle the eye.

sentences.zh: 邪說不去，則正道不興，天下何從治？」

translations.literal: If heterodox doctrines are not removed, then the correct Way cannot rise—how would all under Heaven be governed from?"
translations.idiomatic: Until heresy is cleared away the right Way cannot flourish—how can the realm be governed?"

sentences.zh: 安頓首曰：「陛下所言，可謂深探其本矣。」

translations.literal: An knocked his head and said: "What Your Majesty has spoken may be called deeply probing its root."
translations.idiomatic: An kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty has struck the very root of the matter."

sentences.zh: 安事帝十余歲，視諸儒最舊。

translations.literal: An had served the emperor more than ten years; among the various scholars he was the most senior.
translations.idiomatic: An had served the emperor for more than a decade and was the senior-most of the scholarly counselors.

sentences.zh: 及官侍從，寵愈渥。

translations.literal: When he reached the office of attendant and follower, favor grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the inner circle of attendants, imperial favor only deepened.

sentences.zh: 御制門帖子賜之曰：「國朝謀略無雙士，翰苑文章第一家。」

translations.literal: The emperor in his own hand composed a gate couplet and bestowed it on him, saying: "Of the dynasty's strategists, an unrivaled man; of the Hanlin garden's writings, the foremost family."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally composed a couplet for his gate: "Unrivaled strategist of the dynasty; foremost writer of the academy.

sentences.zh: 時人榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded this as the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 御史或言安隱過。

translations.literal: A censor at times spoke of An's hidden faults.
translations.idiomatic: A censor reported that An had concealed misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝詰曰：「安寧有此，且若何從知？」

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated: "Could An truly have this? Moreover, how did you come to know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded, "Would An truly do such a thing—and how do you know?

sentences.zh: 曰：「聞之道路。」

translations.literal: He said: "I heard it on the road."
translations.idiomatic: The censor answered, "I heard it on the streets."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，立黜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and immediately dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him dismissed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 子晟，洪武中為浙江按察使，以貪賄誅。

translations.literal: His son Cheng in the Hongwu period served as Zhejiang surveillance commissioner and was executed for greed and bribery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao Cheng served as Zhejiang surveillance commissioner in the Hongwu era and was executed for corruption.

sentences.zh: 其兄昱亦坐死。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yu also was implicated and died.
translations.idiomatic: An's elder brother Yu was executed as well by implication.

sentences.zh: 發家屬四十餘人為軍，後死亡且盡。

translations.literal: More than forty members of the household were dispatched as soldiers; later they died and were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty relatives were conscripted as soldiers, and nearly all of them eventually perished.

sentences.zh: 所司復至晟家勾補，安繼妻陳詣闕訴，帝念安功，除其籍。

translations.literal: The responsible office again came to Cheng's household to round up and fill quotas; An's remarried wife Chen went to the palace gates to appeal; the emperor, recalling An's merit, removed her from the register.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities again came to the Cheng household to draft replacements, An's widow, Lady Chen, petitioned at court; remembering An's service, the emperor struck her name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 初，安之裁定諸禮也，廣德錢用壬亦多所論建。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when An drew up the various rites, Qian Yongren of Guangde also contributed many proposals and constructions.
translations.idiomatic: When An first codified the rituals, Qian Yongren of Guangde had also offered extensive guidance.

sentences.zh: 附 錢用壬

translations.literal: Appendix: Qian Yongren
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Qian Yongren

sentences.zh: 用壬，字成夫。

translations.literal: Yongren, style name Chengfuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yongren, styled Chengfuzi.

sentences.zh: 元南榜進士第一，授翰林編修。

translations.literal: He was first on the southern board of Yuan jinshi graduates and was appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the southern metropolitan graduates under the Yuan and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 出使張士誠，留之，授以官。

translations.literal: Sent on a mission to Zhang Shicheng, he was detained and given an office.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Zhang Shicheng he was detained and given a post.

sentences.zh: 大軍下淮、揚，來歸。

translations.literal: When the great army descended on Huai and Yang, he came and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army swept the Huai and Yang regions, he defected to the Ming side.

sentences.zh: 累官御史台經歷，預定律令。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Censorate Manager and participated in fixing codes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become manager of the Censorate secretariat and helped draft the legal codes.

sentences.zh: 尋與陶安等博議郊廟、社稷諸儀。

translations.literal: Soon with Tao An and others he broadly debated suburban sacrifice, ancestral temple, state altar, and other ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Tao An and others in debating suburban sacrifices, temples, and state-altar rites.

sentences.zh: 其議釋奠、耤田，皆援據經文及漢、魏以來故事以定其制。

translations.literal: Their deliberations on the sacrifices to Confucius and the royal plowing all cited classics and precedents from Han and Wei onward to fix their systems.
translations.idiomatic: Their proposals for the Confucian sacrifice and the royal plowing rite drew on the classics and on Han and Wei precedents to set the forms.

sentences.zh: 詔報可，語詳《禮志》。

translations.literal: An edict replied that it was acceptable; the words are detailed in the Ritual Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved these plans; details appear in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年分建六部官，拜用壬禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year one, when the Six Ministries were separately established, Yongren was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongwu year, as the six ministries were organized, Yongren was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡禮儀、祭祀、宴享、貢舉諸政，皆專屬禮官。

translations.literal: All affairs of ritual propriety, sacrifice, banquets, and examinations were solely committed to the ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual conduct, sacrifices, court feasts, and the examination system all fell under the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又詔與儒臣議定乘輿以下冠服諸式。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered him with Confucian ministers to deliberate and fix forms of caps and robes from the imperial carriage downward.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with other scholar-officials to define court dress from the emperor's regalia downward.

sentences.zh: 時儒生多習古義，而用壬考證尤詳確，然其後諸典禮亦多有更定雲。

translations.literal: At the time Confucian scholars mostly studied ancient meanings, but Yongren's textual verification was especially detailed and exact; yet afterward the various canonical rites also had many further revisions, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Many scholars of the day knew ancient precedent, but Yongren's research was especially meticulous; still, many of these rites were later revised again.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，請告歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: That December he asked leave to retire home.

sentences.zh: 詹同，字同文，初名書，婺源人。

translations.literal: Zhan Tong, style name Tongwen, original name Shu, was a man of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Tong, styled Tongwen, born Shu, was from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，學士虞集見之曰：「才子也。」

translations.literal: In youth he was outstandingly clever; Academician Yu Ji seeing him said: "A talent."
translations.idiomatic: He showed exceptional brilliance as a child; the academician Yu Ji exclaimed on meeting him, "A born genius.

sentences.zh: 以其弟槃女妻之。

translations.literal: He gave him in marriage the daughter of his younger brother Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji gave him his younger brother Pan's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 至正中，舉茂才異等，除郴州學正。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng period he was raised as an outstanding maocai and was appointed Chenzhou Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era he was selected as an outstanding talent and made director of studies at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇亂，家黃州，仕陳友諒為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: He encountered disorder, made his home in Huangzhou, and served Chen Youliang as Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil broke out he settled in Huangzhou and served Chen Youliang as chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 太祖下武昌，召為國子博士，賜名同。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Wuchang, he was summoned as National University Erudite and granted the name Tong.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding emperor took Wuchang, he was summoned as a Erudite of the National University and given the name Tong.

sentences.zh: 時功臣子弟教習內府，諸博士治一經，不盡通貫。

translations.literal: At the time sons and younger brothers of meritorious ministers were instructed in the inner palace; the various erudites each handled one classic and did not fully penetrate and connect all.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of meritorious ministers were then tutored in the inner palace, and most erudites taught only one classic without broad mastery.

sentences.zh: 同學識淹博，講《易》、《春秋》最善。

translations.literal: Tong's learning was broad and deep; in lecturing on the Changes and the Spring and Autumn he was best.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's learning was vast; he excelled above all in lecturing on the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 應教為文，才思泉涌，一時莫與並。

translations.literal: When responding to imperial instruction to compose texts, his talent and thought welled forth like a spring—for a time none could stand beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When called on for court compositions, his prose poured forth effortlessly, and for a time no one could rival him.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，直起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Department of Merit Evaluation and served directly on the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Merit Evaluation and served on the Daily Records staff.

sentences.zh: 會議袷禘禮，同議當，遂用之。

translations.literal: When they met to discuss the rites of collective and seasonal sacrifice, Tong's deliberation was appropriate and it was then adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberations on the collective and seasonal sacrifices, Tong's view was adopted.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，與侍御史文原吉、起居注魏觀等循行天下，訪求賢才。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year one, together with Attending Censor Wen Yuanji, Daily Records Wei Guan, and others, he made a circuit of all under Heaven seeking worthy talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongwu year he traveled the realm with the attending censor Wen Yuanji, the recorder Wei Guan, and others to seek out men of talent.

sentences.zh: 還，進翰林直學士，遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: On return he advanced to Hanlin Direct Academician and was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made a direct Hanlin academician and then promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 帝御下峻，御史中丞劉基曰：「古者公卿有罪，盤水加劍，詣請室自裁，所以勵廉恥，存國體也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was stern toward subordinates; Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Ji said: "In antiquity when dukes and ministers had offenses, tray of water and sword were added; they went to the execution chamber to cut themselves short—this was to encourage integrity and shame and preserve the state's stature."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled harshly. Vice censor-in-chief Liu Ji said, "In antiquity, when high ministers offended, they were given a tray of water and a sword and went to the execution chamber to take their own lives—this was how integrity was enforced and the dignity of the state preserved.

sentences.zh: 同時侍側，遂取《戴記》及賈誼疏以進，復剴切言之。

translations.literal: Tong was at the time attending at his side; he thereupon took the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and advanced them, again speaking with earnest incisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, who was attending nearby, cited the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and pressed the point with further earnest argument.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與侍臣言：聲色之害甚於鴆毒，創業之君，為子孫所承式，尤不可不謹。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke to attendant ministers: the harm of sound and color exceeds that of poison wine; a ruler who founds the enterprise is the model his descendants inherit—especially he cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his attendants that the lure of pleasure was deadlier than poison and that a founding ruler, being the model for his heirs, must be doubly careful.

sentences.zh: 同因舉成湯不邇聲色，垂裕後昆以對。

translations.literal: Tong thereupon cited that King Tang did not approach sound and color, extending abundance to his posterity, in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tong answered by citing how King Tang kept his distance from sensual delights to leave a legacy for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 其因事納忠如此。

translations.literal: His offering loyal counsel on occasions was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he offered loyal remonstrance whenever occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 四年進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In year four he advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年兼學士承旨，與學士樂韶鳳定釋奠先師樂章。

translations.literal: In year six he concurrently served as Academician Expositor and with Academician Yue Shaofeng fixed the music for sacrifice at Confucius the first teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he also served as expositor of the Hanlin Academy and, with Academician Yue Shaofeng, set the hymns for sacrifices to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 又以渡江以來，征討平定之跡，禮樂治道之詳，雖有紀載，尚未成書，請編《日曆》。

translations.literal: Also, since the crossing of the Yangzi, the traces of campaigns and pacifications and the details of ritual, music, and governing the Way—though there were records—had not yet become a book; he requested compiling the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that since the Yangzi crossing, records of campaigns and of ritual and governance existed but had not been compiled into a book, and he petitioned to edit an official calendar of the reign.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，命同與宋濂為總裁官，吳伯宗等為纂修官。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; he ordered Tong and Song Lian as chief editors and Wu Bozong and others as compiling editors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed Tong and Song Lian chief compilers, with Wu Bozong and others as editors.

sentences.zh: 七年五月書成，自起兵臨濠至洪武六年，共一百卷。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year seven the book was completed—from raising troops at Linhao to Hongwu year six, altogether one hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished in the fifth month of the seventh year, covering from the raising of forces at Linhao through the sixth Hongwu year in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 同等又言：《日曆》秘天府，人不得見。

translations.literal: Tong and the others further said: the Calendar is secret in the celestial treasury—people cannot see it.
translations.idiomatic: Tong further observed that the Calendar was sealed in the imperial archives and unseen by the public.

sentences.zh: 請仿唐《貞觀政要》，分輯聖政，宣示天下。

translations.literal: They requested, following the Tang Zhenguan Administrative Essentials, to separately compile sagely governance and proclaim it to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that selections of the emperor's governing acts be compiled, as in Tang Essentials of Governance, and published for the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 乃分四十類，凡五卷，名曰《皇明寶訓》。

translations.literal: They then divided into forty categories, altogether five fascicles, entitled Imperial Ming Treasured Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: They arranged the material in forty categories in five juan under the title Treasured Instructions of the August Ming.

sentences.zh: 嗣後凡有政跡，史官日記錄之，隨類增入焉。

translations.literal: Afterward whenever there were governmental traces, historiographers daily recorded them and added them according to category.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter court historians recorded new policies day by day and added them under the appropriate headings.

sentences.zh: 是年賜敕致仕，語極褒美。

translations.literal: That year an edict was granted for retirement; the wording was extremely laudatory.
translations.idiomatic: That year he received an edict granting retirement written in lavish praise.

sentences.zh: 未行，帝覆命與濂議大祀分獻禮。

translations.literal: Before he departed, the emperor again ordered him with Lian to discuss the rites of divided offering at the great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, the emperor recalled him to debate with Song Lian the protocol for associate offerings at the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 久之，起承旨，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised as expositor and died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled as chief expositor and soon died.

sentences.zh: 同以文章結主知，應制占對，靡勿敏贍。

translations.literal: Tong by his writings secured the ruler's trust; responding to imperial compositions and answering extemporaneously, in none was he not nimble and ample.
translations.idiomatic: Tong won the emperor's favor through his prose; in every compositional assignment or impromptu audience he was quick and fluent.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言文章宜明白顯易，通道術，達時務，無取浮薄。

translations.literal: The emperor once said that writings should be clear and plain, open the Way and techniques, reach the affairs of the age, and take nothing frivolous or shallow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said that prose should be plain and accessible, convey practical governance, speak to current affairs, and avoid empty ornament.

sentences.zh: 同所為多稱旨，而操行尤耿介，故至老眷注不衰。

translations.literal: What Tong composed mostly pleased the intent, and his conduct was especially upright and unyielding, so even to old age imperial regard did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: His compositions usually pleased the emperor, and his conduct was notably upright, so imperial favor never waned even in his old age.

sentences.zh: 子徽，字資善，洪武十五年舉秀才。

translations.literal: His son Hui, style name Zishan, in Hongwu year fifteen was raised as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhan Hui, styled Zishan, passed the xiucai examination in the fifteenth Hongwu year.

sentences.zh: 官至太子少保兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His office reached Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 有才智，剛決不可犯。

translations.literal: He had talent and wisdom; firm and decisive, he could not be transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: He was capable and resolute, and brooked no challenge.

sentences.zh: 勤於治事，為帝所獎任。

translations.literal: Diligent in governing affairs, he was rewarded and entrusted by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He worked tirelessly at administration and won the emperor's trust and praise.

sentences.zh: 然性險刻。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature harsh and unforgiving.

sentences.zh: 李善長之死，徽有力焉。

translations.literal: In Li Shanchang's death, Hui had force in it.
translations.idiomatic: He played a significant part in Li Shanchang's downfall and death.

sentences.zh: 藍玉下獄，語連徽及子尚寶丞紱，並坐誅。

translations.literal: When Lan Yu was imprisoned, words implicated Hui and his son, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Fu, and both were executed by implication.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Yu was imprisoned, the case implicated Hui and his son Fu, a vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; both were executed.

sentences.zh: 同從孫希原，為中書舍人，善大書。

translations.literal: Tong's collateral descendant by a younger branch, Xiyuan, was a Secretariat Drafter, skilled in large script.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's grandnephew Xiyuan served as a drafter in the Secretariat and excelled at large-character calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 宮殿城門題額，往往皆希原筆也。

translations.literal: Inscriptions for palace gates and city gates were often Xiyuan's brush.
translations.idiomatic: Many gate inscriptions throughout the palaces and city walls were in his hand.

sentences.zh: 朱升，字允升，休寧人。

translations.literal: Zhu Sheng, style name Yunsheng, was a man of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sheng, styled Yunsheng, was from Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 元末舉鄉薦，為池州學正，講授有法。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he was recommended in the provincial selection, became Instructor of Chizhou, and lectured with method.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan he was recommended in the provincial examination, became director of studies at Chizhou, and taught with notable discipline.

sentences.zh: 蘄、黃盜起，棄官隱石門。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Qi and Huang, he abandoned office and hid at Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels spread through Qi and Huang, he resigned and went into seclusion at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 數避兵逋竄，卒未嘗一日廢學。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he fled warfare and hid, yet in the end he never let a single day pass without study.
translations.idiomatic: Though he fled repeatedly from warfare, he never let a single day pass without study.

sentences.zh: 太祖下徽州，以鄧愈薦，召問時務。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Huizhou, on Deng Yu's recommendation he was summoned and asked about the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took Huizhou, Deng Yu recommended him; he was summoned and questioned on current strategy.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「高築牆，廣積糧，緩稱王。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Build high walls, amass grain widely, and be slow to declare yourself king.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Build high walls, store grain in abundance, and declare kingship only when the time is ripe.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with this counsel.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，授侍講學士，知制誥，同修國史。

translations.literal: In the first Wu year he was appointed Reader-in-Waiting, drafted imperial proclamations, and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Wu year he was made reader-in-waiting, charged with drafting edicts, and helped compile the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 以年老，特免朝謁。

translations.literal: Because of advanced age he was specially exempted from court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age he was specially excused from attending court.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年進翰林學士，定宗廟時享齋戒之禮。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year one he advanced to Hanlin Academician and fixed the rites of fasting and purification for ancestral temple seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongwu year he was promoted to Hanlin academician and set the fasting rules for ancestral temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋命與諸儒修《女誡》，採古賢后妃事可法者編上之。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered with various Confucians to revise the Admonitions for Women, selecting from antiquity empresses and consorts whose deeds could serve as models and compiling them for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered with other scholars to compile the Admonitions for Women from exemplary empresses and consorts of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 大封功臣，制詞多升撰，時稱典核。

translations.literal: When meritorious ministers were greatly enfeoffed, many encomia were composed by Sheng; men of the time called them canonical and exact.
translations.idiomatic: When the great enfeoffments were proclaimed, Sheng drafted many of the patent texts, which contemporaries praised as models of precision.

sentences.zh: 逾年，請老歸，卒年七十二。

translations.literal: After more than a year he requested to retire and return home; he died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to retire home and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 升自幼力學，至老不倦。

translations.literal: From youth Sheng exerted himself in learning; to old age he did not weary.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had studied strenuously from childhood and never slackened even in old age.

sentences.zh: 尤邃經學。

translations.literal: He was especially penetrating in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially profound in classical studies.

sentences.zh: 所作諸經旁注，辭約義精。

translations.literal: The collateral commentaries on the classics that he composed were brief in wording yet precise in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral commentaries on the classics were concise in language yet exact in meaning.

sentences.zh: 學者稱楓林先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Fenglin.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars called him Master Fenglin.

sentences.zh: 子同官禮部侍郎，坐事死。

translations.literal: His son Tong held office as Vice Minister of Rites and died by implication in an offense.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu Tong served as vice minister of rites and was executed after being implicated in a case.

sentences.zh: 二年，議上仁祖陵曰「英陵」，復請行祭告禮。

translations.literal: In year two they deliberated raising the tomb of the benevolent ancestor to the title Ying Mausoleum and again requested performing the announcement sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year officials proposed naming the founding emperor's father's tomb Ying Mausoleum and petitioned to perform an announcement sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太常博士孫吾與以漢、唐未有行者，駁之。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite Sun Luyu, on the ground that Han and Tang had no precedent for such action, rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Sun Luyu objected that Han and Tang had no precedent for this.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「漢光武加先陵曰『昌』，宋太祖亦加高祖陵曰『欽』，曾祖陵曰『康』，祖陵曰『定』，考陵曰『安』，蓋創業之君尊其祖考，則亦尊崇其陵。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Emperor Guangwu of Han added to his forefather's tomb the name Chang; Emperor Taizu of Song also added to his high ancestor's tomb the name Qin, his great-grandfather's tomb Kang, his grandfather's tomb Ding, and his father's tomb An—generally a ruler who founds the enterprise honors his forefathers, and then also honors their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied, "Emperor Guangwu of Han styled his forefather's tomb Chang; the Song founder likewise styled his ancestors' tombs Qin, Kang, Ding, and An. Founding rulers honor their forebears and therefore honor their tombs as well.

sentences.zh: 既尊其陵，自應祭告，禮固緣人情而起者也。」

translations.literal: Having honored the tomb, one should naturally perform announcement sacrifice; ritual indeed arises from human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Once the tomb is honored, an announcement sacrifice is fitting, for ritual springs from human sentiment.

sentences.zh: 廷議是亮。

translations.literal: The court deliberation approved Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sided with Liang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，亮言：「《禮運》曰『禮行於郊，則百神受職。』

translations.literal: Shortly after, Liang said: "The Ritual Operations says, When ritual is performed in the suburbs, then the hundred spirits receive their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liang cited the Ritual Operations: "When ritual is performed in the suburbs, the hundred spirits receive their offices.

sentences.zh: 今宜增天下神祗壇於圜丘之東，方澤之西。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to add an altar to all spirits under Heaven east of the Round Mound and west of the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed adding an altar to all spirits under Heaven east of the Round Mound and west of the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 又言：「《郊特牲》『器用陶匏』，《周禮疏》『外祀用瓦』。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Special Sacrifices states that vessels use pottery and gourds; the Zhou Rites commentary states that outer sacrifices use tile.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited the Special Sacrifices on pottery vessels and the Zhou Rites commentary on tile vessels for outer sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今祭祀用瓷，與古意合。

translations.literal: Now sacrifices use porcelain, which accords with ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that present sacrifices used porcelain, in keeping with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 而槃盂之屬，與古尚異，宜皆易以瓷，惟籩用竹。」

translations.literal: Yet platters and bowls and the like still differ from antiquity; all should be changed to porcelain, only the bian baskets using bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: Platters and bowls still differed from antiquity; he urged replacing them with porcelain, retaining bamboo only for the bian baskets."

sentences.zh: 又請大祀前七日，陪祀官詣中書受誓戒，戒辭如唐禮。

translations.literal: He also requested that seven days before the great sacrifice, associate sacrificers go to the Secretariat to receive oath and abstinence; the abstinence wording should follow Tang ritual."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that associate sacrificers receive oath and abstinence at the Secretariat seven days before the great sacrifice, following Tang formulas."

sentences.zh: 又依《周禮》定五祀及四時薦新、稞禮、圭瓚、郁鬯之制。

translations.literal: He also according to the Zhou Rites fixed the five sacrifices and seasonal new offerings, libation rites, jade scepter and libation cup, and scented libation regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Zhou Rites, he also defined the five sacrifices, seasonal offerings, libation rites, and regalia for jade scepter and scented libation.

sentences.zh: 並言旗纛月朔望致祭，煩而瀆，宜止，行於當祭之月。

translations.literal: He also said that offering sacrifice to banners and standards on the new and full moon was troublesome and irreverent and should cease, being performed only in the month when sacrifice was due.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that monthly sacrifices to military banners were burdensome and irreverent and should be held only in the relevant sacrificial month.

sentences.zh: 皆允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂亮：「先賢有言：『見其生不忍見其死，聞其聲不忍食其肉。』

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Liang: "The sages of antiquity said: Seeing them alive one cannot bear to see them die; hearing their sounds one cannot bear to eat their flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Liang, "The ancients said that seeing animals alive one cannot bear to see them slaughtered, and hearing their cries one cannot bear to eat their flesh.

sentences.zh: 今祭祀省牲於神壇甚邇，心殊未安。」

translations.literal: Now in sacrifice the sparing of the victim is very close to the spirit altar; the heart is especially not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today the inspection of sacrificial animals takes place very near the altar, which troubles me deeply.

sentences.zh: 亮乃奏考古省牲之儀，遠神壇二百步。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon memorialized examining the ancient rite of sparing victims, two hundred paces from the spirit altar.
translations.idiomatic: Liang researched the ancient rite and memorialized that victims should be inspected two hundred paces from the altar.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 帝慮郊社諸祭，壇而不屋，或驟雨沾服。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that for suburban and community sacrifices, altars without halls—or sudden rain—might soak the robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that suburban sacrifices, being performed on open altars without halls, might leave participants drenched in sudden rain.

sentences.zh: 亮引宋祥符九年南郊遇雨，於太尉廳望祭，及元《經世大典》壇垣內外建屋避風雨故事，奏之。

translations.literal: Liang cited the Song Xiangfu ninth year when the southern suburban sacrifice met rain and sacrifice was performed looking from the Grand Marshal's hall, and the Yuan Comprehensive Institutions of the Ages precedent of building houses within and without the altar enclosure to avoid wind and rain, and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang cited the Song precedent of performing a rain-delayed suburban sacrifice from the Grand Marshal's hall in Xiangfu 9 and Yuan regulations for shelter within the altar precinct, and memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遂詔：建殿於壇南，遇雨則望祭。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered: build a hall south of the altar; when rain comes then perform looking sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a hall built south of the altar; when it rained, sacrifice would be performed from there.

sentences.zh: 而靈星諸祠亦皆因亮言建壇屋焉。

translations.literal: The various shrines such as the Spirit Star also all because of Liang's words had altar halls built.
translations.idiomatic: Altar halls were likewise built for the Spirit Star and other shrines on Liang's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時仁祖已配南北郊，而郊祀禮成後，復詣太廟恭謝。

translations.literal: At the time the benevolent ancestor was already associated at the southern and northern suburbs, yet after suburban sacrifice rites were completed they again went to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to offer respectful thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's spirit had been enshrined at both suburban altars, yet after suburban rites the court still went to the Ancestral Temple to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 亮言宜罷，惟先祭三日，詣太廟以配享告。

translations.literal: Liang said this should be stopped; only three days before sacrifice should one go to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to announce the associated offering.
translations.idiomatic: Liang urged ending this practice, leaving only a visit three days beforehand to announce the associated offering.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 帝以日中有黑子，疑祭天不順所致，欲增郊壇從祀之神。

translations.literal: The emperor, because there was a black spot in the sun, suspected it came from improper sacrifice to Heaven and wished to increase the spirits associated at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: When a black spot appeared on the sun, the emperor suspected faulty heavenly sacrifice and considered adding more associated deities at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 亮執奏：漢、唐煩瀆，不宜取法。

translations.literal: Liang firmly memorialized: Han and Tang were troublesome and irreverent—not fitting to take as models.
translations.idiomatic: Liang firmly objected that Han and Tang practice had been excessive and should not be imitated.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝一日問亮曰：「朕郊祀天地，拜位正中，而百官朝參則班列東西，何也？」

translations.literal: One day the emperor asked Liang: "When I sacrifice to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs, my bowing position is directly centered, yet when the hundred officials attend court they form ranks east and west—why?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked Liang, "At suburban sacrifice I bow from the center, yet at court audiences officials stand east and west—why is that?

sentences.zh: 亮對曰：「天子祭天，升自午陛，北向，答陽之義也；

translations.literal: Liang replied: "The Son of Heaven sacrificing to Heaven ascends by the noon steps and faces north, answering the meaning of yang;
translations.idiomatic: Liang answered, "The Son of Heaven ascends the noon steps and faces north when sacrificing to Heaven, answering the principle of yang;

sentences.zh: 祭社，升自子陛，南向，答陰之義也。

translations.literal: sacrificing to the soil god, he ascends by the zi steps and faces south, answering the meaning of yin.
translations.idiomatic: when sacrificing to Earth he ascends the zi steps and faces south, answering the principle of yin.

sentences.zh: 若群臣朝參，當避君上之尊，故升降皆由卯陛，朝班分列東西，以避馳道，其義不同。」

translations.literal: If the various ministers attend court, they should avoid the ruler's exalted position; therefore ascending and descending are all by the mao steps, and court ranks are divided east and west to avoid the imperial roadway—the meanings differ."
translations.idiomatic: For court audiences ministers must avoid the ruler's position of honor, so they use the mao steps and stand east and west to avoid the imperial roadway—the meanings differ."

sentences.zh: 亮倉卒占對，必傅經義，多此類。

translations.literal: Liang in haste improvising replies always attached to classical meaning; many were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's impromptu replies always cited classical principle; this was typical of his manner.

sentences.zh: 自郊廟祭祀外，朝賀山呼、百司箋奏、上下冠服、殿上坐墩諸儀及大射軍禮，皆亮所酌定。

translations.literal: Apart from suburban and temple sacrifice, court congratulations and mountain calls, the hundred offices' memorials, caps and robes above and below, hall seating cushions, and great archery military ritual were all weighed and fixed by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond suburban and temple rites, Liang also set court congratulations, the hundred offices' memorial protocol, court dress, hall seating, and great archery military ritual.

sentences.zh: 惟言「大祀帝親省牲，中祀、小祀之牲當遣官代」，帝命：「親祭者皆親省」。

translations.literal: Only he said that at great sacrifice the emperor personally inspects victims, but at medium and small sacrifice the victims should be sent for officials to replace—the emperor ordered: "For sacrifices one personally attends, all personally inspect."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that only the emperor inspect victims at great sacrifices while officials should do so at lesser ones, but the emperor ruled that any sacrifice he attended required his personal inspection.

sentences.zh: 又請依唐制，令郡國奏祥瑞。

translations.literal: He also requested following Tang institutions to order commanderies and states to memorialize auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, following Tang practice, that commanderies report auspicious omens.

sentences.zh: 帝以災異所系尤重，命有司驛聞，與亮議異焉。

translations.literal: The emperor held that portents of disaster and anomaly were especially weighty and ordered responsible offices to report by post relay; this differed from Liang's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, placing greater weight on reports of disasters and anomalies, ordered rapid relay of such news—diverging from Liang's view.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year three he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 其後牛諒、答祿與權、張籌、牛夢炎、劉仲質之屬，亦各有所論建。

translations.literal: Afterward Niu Liang, Dalu Youquan, Zhang Chou, Niu Mengyan, Liu Zhongzhi, and their kind also each had proposals and constructions.
translations.idiomatic: Later Niu Liang, Dalu Youquan, Zhang Chou, Niu Mengyan, Liu Zhongzhi, and others likewise offered ritual proposals.

sentences.zh: 附 牛諒

translations.literal: Appendix: Niu Liang
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Niu Liang

sentences.zh: 牛諒，字士良，東平人。

translations.literal: Niu Liang, style name Shiliang, was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Liang, styled Shiliang, was from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，舉秀才，為典簿。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year one he was raised as xiucai and became Records Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongwu year he passed the xiucai examination and became a records clerk.

sentences.zh: 與張以寧使安南還，稱旨，三遷至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Yining he was envoy to Annan; on return he pleased the intent and was thrice promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After serving with Zhang Yining as envoy to Annan and pleasing the emperor on his return, he was thrice promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 更定釋奠及大祀分獻禮，與詹同等議省牲、冠服。

translations.literal: He revised the Confucian sacrifice and great-sacrifice divided-offering rites, and with Zhan Tong and others deliberated sparing victims and caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the Confucian sacrifice and great-sacrifice associate-offering rites and, with Zhan Tong and others, debated victim inspection and court dress.

sentences.zh: 御史答祿與權請祀三皇。

translations.literal: Censor Dalu Youquan requested sacrifice to the Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Dalu Youquan petitioned to sacrifice to the Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 太祖下其議禮官，並命考歷代帝王有功德者廟祀之。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor sent their deliberation to ritual officials and also ordered examining which emperors through the ages had merit and virtue for temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor referred the matter to ritual officials and ordered a survey of meritorious emperors worthy of temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，諒奏：三皇立廟京師，春秋致祭。

translations.literal: In the first month of year seven Liang memorialized: the Three Sovereigns should have a temple established in the capital with spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Liang memorialized that a Three Sovereigns temple should be built in the capital with spring and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐以下，就陵立廟。

translations.literal: From Han and Tang downward, temples were established at their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: For Han and Tang emperors onward, temples were established at their tombs.

sentences.zh: 帝為更定行之，亦詳《禮志》。

translations.literal: The emperor revised and fixed this for implementation; details are in the Ritual Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revised and implemented the system; details appear in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 是年怠職，降主事。

translations.literal: That year, for neglect of duty, he was demoted to Section Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was demoted to section chief for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復官。

translations.literal: Before long his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 後仍以不任職罷。

translations.literal: Later he was again dismissed for incompetence in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed again for incompetence.

sentences.zh: 諒著述甚多，為世傳誦。

translations.literal: Liang's writings were very numerous and were transmitted and recited by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liang wrote extensively, and his works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 附 答祿與權

translations.literal: Appendix: Dalu Youquan
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Dalu Youquan

sentences.zh: 答祿與權，字道夫，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Dalu Youquan, style name Daofu, was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Dalu Youquan, styled Daofu, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 仕元為河南北道廉訪司僉事。

translations.literal: Under Yuan he served as Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Henan North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan he served as surveillance vice commissioner on the Henan North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入明，寓河南永寧。

translations.literal: Entering Ming, he resided at Yongning in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming founding he lived at Yongning in Henan.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，用薦授秦府紀善，改御史。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year six, on recommendation he was appointed Chronicler of the Qin Princely Establishment, then changed to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth Hongwu year, on recommendation, he was appointed chronicler of the Qin princely establishment and later made a censor.

sentences.zh: 請重刊律令。

translations.literal: He requested reprinting the codes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to reprint the legal codes.

sentences.zh: 盱眙民進瑞麥，與權請薦宗廟。

translations.literal: The people of Xuyi presented auspicious wheat; Youquan requested offering it to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Xuyi presented auspicious wheat, Youquan asked that it be offered at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以瑞麥為朕德所致，朕不敢當。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To take auspicious wheat as caused by my virtue—I dare not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To treat this wheat as proof of my virtue is more than I dare claim.

sentences.zh: 其必歸之祖宗。

translations.literal: It must certainly be attributed to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: It must be credited to the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 御史言是也。」

translations.literal: The censor's words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The censor is correct.

sentences.zh: 明年出為廣西按察僉事。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as surveillance vice commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 未行，復為御史。

translations.literal: Before departing he was again made Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was made censor again.

sentences.zh: 上書請祀三皇。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting sacrifice to the Three Sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again requesting sacrifice to the Three Sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 下禮官議，遂並建帝王廟。

translations.literal: Sent down to ritual officials for deliberation, they then together built the Imperial Emperors Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to ritual officials, and the Imperial Emperors Temple was established.

sentences.zh: 且遣使者巡視歷代諸陵寢。

translations.literal: Moreover envoys were dispatched to inspect the tombs and mausoleums of successive ages.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were also sent to inspect the tombs of emperors through the ages.

sentences.zh: 設守陵戶二人，三年一祭，其制皆由此始。

translations.literal: Two tomb-guard households were established; sacrifice every three years—the system all began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Two guard households were assigned to each tomb, with sacrifices every three years—a system that began with this initiative.

sentences.zh: 又請行禘禮，議格不行。

translations.literal: He also requested performing the di sacrifice; deliberation was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed performing the di sacrifice, but deliberation blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 改翰林修撰，坐事降典籍，尋進應奉。

translations.literal: Changed to Hanlin Compiler; for an offense demoted to Archivist, soon advanced to Responding to Imperial Composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin compiler, demoted to archivist after an offense, and soon promoted to responding to imperial composition.

sentences.zh: 十一年以年老致仕。

translations.literal: In year eleven, because of advanced age he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 禘禮至嘉靖中始定。

translations.literal: The di sacrifice was fixed only in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: The di sacrifice was not finally settled until the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 附 張籌

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhang Chou
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Zhang Chou

sentences.zh: 張籌，字惟中，無錫人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chou, style name Weizhong, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chou, styled Weizhong, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 父翼，嘗勸張士誠將莫天佑降，復請於平章胡美勿僇降人，城中人得完。

translations.literal: His father Yi had once urged Zhang Shicheng to have Mo Tianyou submit, and again requested of Pacification Commissioner Hu Mei not to slaughter those who surrendered, so the people in the city were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yi had urged Zhang Shicheng to accept Mo Tianyou's surrender and persuaded Commissioner Hu Mei not to massacre the surrendered, sparing the city's population.

sentences.zh: 以詹同薦，授翰林應奉，改禮部主事。

translations.literal: On Zhan Tong's recommendation he was appointed Hanlin Responding to Imperial Composition and changed to Ritual Department Section Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Zhan Tong, he was appointed to respond to imperial compositions in the Hanlin Academy and later made a section chief in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奉詔與尚書陶凱編集漢、唐以來籓王事跡，為《歸鑒錄》。

translations.literal: By imperial command together with Minister Tao Kai he compiled deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward, making the Returning Mirror Record.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he and Minister Tao Kai compiled the deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward into the Returning Mirror Record.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，由員外郎進尚書，與學士宋濂定諸王妃喪服之制。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year nine, from Vice Director he advanced to Minister and with Academician Song Lian fixed the mourning-garb system for various princely consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth Hongwu year he rose from vice director to minister and, with Song Lian, set mourning regulations for princely consorts.

sentences.zh: 籌記誦淹博，在禮曹久，諳於歷代禮文沿革。

translations.literal: Chou's memory and recitation were broad and deep; long in the Ritual Office, he was thoroughly versed in the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Chou had a prodigious memory; after long service in the Ministry of Rites he knew the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.

sentences.zh: 然頗善附會。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather good at forced interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was inclined to force classical texts to fit present needs.

sentences.zh: 初，陶安等定圜丘、方澤、宗廟、社稷諸儀，行數年矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning Tao An and others had fixed the rites of the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altar, and they had been practiced several years.
translations.idiomatic: Tao An and others had years earlier set rites for the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altars.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，籌為尚書，乃更議合社稷為一壇，罷勾龍、棄配位，奉仁祖配饗，以明祖社尊而親之之道，遂以社稷與郊廟祀並列上祀。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year nine Chou became Minister and then again deliberated merging the state altars into one altar, abolishing the associated positions of Gou Long and Qi, offering the benevolent ancestor as associated sacrifice, to clarify the Way of honoring the state altars while treating them as kin—and thus placed the state altars in upper sacrifice alongside suburban and temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: As minister in the ninth year Chou merged the altars of soil and grain into one, removed Gou Long and Qi from associated worship, and enshrined the founding emperor's father there, elevating the state altars to the highest tier of sacrifice alongside suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 識者竊非之。

translations.literal: Men of insight privately disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledgeable observers quietly disapproved.

sentences.zh: 已，出為湖廣參政。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as administrative commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十年坐事罰輸作。

translations.literal: In year ten for an offense he was penalized to perform labor service.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was sentenced to corvée labor for an offense.

sentences.zh: 十二年仍起禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: In year twelve he was still raised as Ritual Department Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 後復官，以事免。

translations.literal: Later his office was restored again; for an affair he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed but dismissed again after another incident.

sentences.zh: 附 硃夢炎

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhu Mengyan
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Zhu Mengyan

sentences.zh: 硃夢炎，字仲雅，進賢人。

translations.literal: Zhu Mengyan, style name Zhongya, was a man of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mengyan, styled Zhongya, was from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 元進士，為金谿丞。

translations.literal: A Yuan jinshi, he was magistrate of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuan jinshi, he served as magistrate of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 太祖召居賓館，命與熊鼎集古事，為質直語，教公卿子弟，名曰《公子書》。

translations.literal: The Taizu emperor summoned him to lodge at the guest house and ordered him with Xiong Ding to collect ancient matters into straightforward language to teach the sons of dukes and ministers, entitled Book for the Lord's Sons.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor lodged him at the guest residence and ordered him and Xiong Ding to compile ancient exempla in plain language for educating noble sons, titled Book for the Lord's Sons.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，自禮部侍郎進尚書。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year eleven, from Vice Minister of Rites he advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh Hongwu year he rose from vice minister to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 帝方稽古右文，夢炎援古證今，剖析源流，如指諸掌，文章詳雅有根據。

translations.literal: The emperor was at the time examining antiquity and honoring literature; Mengyan cited antiquity to prove the present and analyzed origins and currents as if pointing at his palm—his writings detailed, elegant, and grounded.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor promoted classical learning, Mengyan cited antiquity to illuminate the present with encyclopedic clarity; his essays were elegant and well founded.

sentences.zh: 帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 附 劉仲質

translations.literal: Appendix: Liu Zhongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Appendix — Liu Zhongzhi

sentences.zh: 劉仲質，字文質，分宜人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongzhi, style name Wenzhi, was a man of Fenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongzhi, styled Wenzhi, was from Fenyi.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以宜春訓導薦入京，擢翰林典籍，奉命校正《春秋本末》。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu, recommended as Yichun Instructor, he was raised to the capital, promoted to Hanlin Archivist, and ordered to collate the Beginning and End of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu, recommended as instructor at Yichun, he was brought to court, made Hanlin archivist, and ordered to collate the Beginning and End of the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 十五年拜禮部尚書，命與儒臣定釋奠禮，頒行天下學校。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he was appointed Minister of Rites and ordered with Confucian ministers to fix the Confucian sacrifice rite and promulgate it to schools throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became minister of rites and, with other scholars, fixed the Confucian sacrifice for schools empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 每歲春秋仲月，通禮孔子如儀。

translations.literal: Each year in the second months of spring and autumn, Confucius was honored with full ritual as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn the second month, Confucius was honored with the full ritual.

sentences.zh: 時國子學新成，帝將行釋菜。

translations.literal: At the time the National University was newly completed and the emperor was about to perform the vegetable offering.
translations.idiomatic: When the National University was newly completed, the emperor was to perform the vegetable offering.

sentences.zh: 侍臣有言：孔子雖聖，人臣也，禮宜一奠再拜。

translations.literal: Attendant ministers said: although Confucius was a sage, he was a subject; ritual should be one offering and two bows.
translations.idiomatic: Some attendants argued that although Confucius was a sage he remained a subject and deserved only one offering and two bows.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔周太祖如孔子廟，左右謂不宜拜。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the past the Zhou founder went to Confucius's temple; those at his left and right said it was not fitting to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the Zhou founder visited Confucius's temple, his attendants said he should not bow.

sentences.zh: 周太祖曰：『孔子，百世帝王師，何敢不拜！』

translations.literal: The Zhou founder said: "Confucius is teacher to emperors through the hundred generations—how dare I not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: The founder replied, "Confucius is teacher to emperors for a hundred generations—how dare I not bow!"

sentences.zh: 今朕有天下，敬禮百神，於先師禮宜加崇。」

translations.literal: Now I possess all under Heaven and respectfully honor the hundred spirits; toward the first teacher the ritual should be further elevated."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I possess the realm, I honor all spirits; toward the first teacher the rite should be still more exalted.

sentences.zh: 乃命仲質詳議。

translations.literal: He then ordered Zhongzhi to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhongzhi to work out the details.

sentences.zh: 仲質請帝服皮弁執圭，詣先師位前，再拜，獻爵，又再拜，退易服。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi requested that the emperor wear the leather cap and hold the jade tablet, go before the first teacher's position, bow twice, present the libation cup, bow twice again, then withdraw and change robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi proposed that the emperor wear the leather cap and hold the jade tablet, bow twice before Confucius, present the libation cup, bow twice again, then withdraw and change robes.

sentences.zh: 乃詣彝倫堂命講，庶典禮隆重。

translations.literal: Then go to the Hall of Moral Principles and order lecturing, so that the canonical rites would be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: He would then proceed to the Hall of Moral Principles to order lectures, lending the ceremony full dignity.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又立學規十二條，合欽定九條，頒賜師生。

translations.literal: He also established twelve school regulations, combined with nine imperially approved articles, and bestowed them on teachers and students.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued twelve school regulations, combined with nine imperial articles, for teachers and students.

sentences.zh: 已，復奉命頒劉向《說苑》、《新序》於學校，令生員講讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to distribute Liu Xiang's Garden of Sayings and New Prefaces to schools, ordering students to lecture and read them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to distribute Liu Xiang's Garden of Sayings and New Prefaces to schools for student study.

sentences.zh: 是年冬改華蓋殿大學士，帝為親制誥文。

translations.literal: That winter he was changed to Grand Academician of the Huagai Hall; the emperor personally composed the patent text.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made grand academician of the Huagai Hall, with an encomium drafted by the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶御史。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to censor after an offense.

sentences.zh: 後以老致仕。

translations.literal: Later he retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 仲質為人厚重篤實，博通經史，文體典確，常當帝意焉。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi as a man was weighty, sincere, and solid; broadly penetrating classics and histories; his literary style canonical and exact—he often matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi was grave and sincere, versed in classics and histories; his dignified prose usually pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 陶凱，字中立，臨海人。

translations.literal: Tao Kai, style name Zhongli, was a man of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kai, styled Zhongli, was from Linhai.

sentences.zh: 領至正鄉薦，除永豐教諭，不就。

translations.literal: He led the Zhizheng provincial recommendation, was appointed Instructor of Yongfeng, and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the Zhizheng provincial list and was appointed instructor at Yongfeng, but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以薦征入，同修《元史》。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu, on recommendation he was summoned in and concurrently edited the History of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he was summoned on recommendation and helped compile the History of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 書成，授翰林應奉，教習大本堂，授楚王經。

translations.literal: When the book was completed he was appointed Hanlin Responding to Imperial Composition, instructed at the Great Foundation Hall, and taught the Prince of Chu the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was finished he became a Hanlin responder, taught at the Great Foundation Hall, and instructed the Prince of Chu in the classics.

sentences.zh: 三年七月與崔亮併為禮部尚書，各有敷奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of year three he and Cui Liang together became Ministers of Rites; each had memorials and presentations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he and Cui Liang were jointly appointed ministers of rites, each submitting ritual proposals.

sentences.zh: 軍禮及品官墳塋之制，凱議也。

translations.literal: Military ritual and the system for ranked officials' tombs and graveyards were Kai's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Military ritual and regulations for officials' tombs were Kai's work.

sentences.zh: 其年，亮卒。

translations.literal: That year Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang died that year.

sentences.zh: 凱獨任，定科舉式。

translations.literal: Kai alone bore the responsibility and fixed the examination format.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then bore sole responsibility and set the civil service examination format.

sentences.zh: 明年會試，以凱充主考官，取吳伯宗等百二十人程文進御，凱序其首簡，遂為定例。

translations.literal: The next year at the metropolitan examination Kai served as chief examiner; he took Wu Bozong and one hundred twenty others' examination essays and presented them to the throne; Kai composed the preface to the top essay—and this became the fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The next metropolitan examination made Kai chief examiner; he presented the papers of Wu Bozong and 120 others to the throne and wrote the preface to the top essay, establishing a lasting precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭凱曰：「事死如事生，朕養已不逮，宜盡追遠之道。」

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed Kai: "Serving the dead as serving the living—I in nurturing have not reached them; I should exhaust the Way of pursuing the distant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Kai, "One should serve the dead as the living; I have not adequately provided for my forebears and must observe every rite of remembrance.

sentences.zh: 凱以太廟已有常祀，乃請於乾清宮左別建奉先殿，以奉神御。

translations.literal: Kai, because the Imperial Ancestral Temple already had regular sacrifice, then requested building separately to the left of the Qianqing Palace a Hall for Venerating Ancestors to enshrine spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ancestral temple already had regular sacrifices, Kai proposed building a Hall for Venerating Ancestors east of the Qianqing Palace to house spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 明奉先殿之制自此始。

translations.literal: The Ming system of the Hall for Venerating Ancestors began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming hall-of-ancestors system began here.

sentences.zh: 五年，凱言：「漢、唐、宋時皆有會要，紀載時政。

translations.literal: In year five Kai said: "Han, Tang, and Song all had institutional summaries recording the politics of the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Kai noted that Han, Tang, and Song had all kept institutional summaries of current governance.

sentences.zh: 今起居注雖設，其諸司所領諭旨及奏事簿籍，宜依會要，編類為書，庶可以垂法後世。

translations.literal: Now although the Daily Records are established, the various offices' received edicts and memorial affair registers should follow the institutional summary, compiled by category into books, so that they might hand down models to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that edicts and memorial registers from each office be compiled by category, like those summaries, to preserve models for posterity.

sentences.zh: 下臺省府者，宜各置銅櫃藏之，以備稽考，俾無遺闕。」

translations.literal: Those sent down to the Secretariat and ministries should each set up bronze cabinets to store them for examination, so that nothing is lost or omitted."
translations.idiomatic: Offices receiving imperial orders should keep bronze cabinets of records for audit so nothing would be lost.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，出為湖廣參政。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he went out as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was posted to Huguang as administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired.

sentences.zh: 八年起為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In year eight he was raised as Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 明年改晉王府左相。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Left Counselor of the Prince of Jin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became left counselor to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 凱博學，工詩文。

translations.literal: Kai was broadly learned and skilled in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was erudite and accomplished in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗厭前代樂章多諛辭，或未雅馴，命凱與詹同更撰，甚稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor once grew weary that former dynasties' ritual hymns had many flattering words or were not elegant and well trained, and ordered Kai with Zhan Tong to rewrite them anew—greatly pleasing the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, disliking the flattery and roughness of earlier dynastic hymns, ordered Kai and Zhan Tong to rewrite them to great approval.

sentences.zh: 長至侍齋宮，言：宜有篇什以紀慶成。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice attending the fasting palace, he said there should be a piece to record the completion of the celebration.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice, attending the fasting palace, he suggested composing verses to mark the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 遂命凱首唱，諸臣俱和，而宋濂為之序。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Kai to lead the singing; the various ministers all harmonized, and Song Lian wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Kai lead the composition while other ministers harmonized and Song Lian wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 其後扈行陪祀，有所獻，帝輒稱善。

translations.literal: Afterward when accompanying on journeys and attending sacrifice, whenever he presented something the emperor always praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever he accompanied sacrifices and presented writings, the emperor praised them.

sentences.zh: 一時詔令、封冊、歌頌、碑誌多出其手雲。

translations.literal: For a time edicts, enfeoffments, odes, and stele inscriptions mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: For a time most edicts, patents, hymns, and epitaphs came from his brush.

sentences.zh: 凱嘗自號「耐久道人」。

translations.literal: Kai once styled himself "The Long-Enduring Daoist."
translations.idiomatic: Kai once styled himself "the Long-Enduring Daoist."

sentences.zh: 帝聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor hearing this detested it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 坐在禮部時朝使往高麗主客曹誤用符驗，論死。

translations.literal: He sat in an offense from when at the Ministry of Rites an envoy to Goryeo mistakenly used credentials at the Reception Office; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Ministry of Rites, an envoy to Goryeo misused credentials at the reception office; Kai was sentenced to death on this charge.

sentences.zh: 曾魯，字得之，新淦人。

translations.literal: Zeng Lu, style name Dezhi, was a man of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Lu, styled Dezhi, was from Xingan.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，能暗誦《五經》，一字不遺。

translations.literal: At age seven he could recite the Five Classics from memory without losing a single character.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could recite the Five Classics from memory without omitting a character.

sentences.zh: 稍長，博通古今。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown, he broadly penetrated past and present.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he mastered history ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 凡數千年國體、人才，制度沿革，無不能言者。

translations.literal: Whatever of several thousand years' state structure, talented men, and institutional evolution—none could he not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: He could discourse on institutions, eminent men, and reforms across thousands of years.

sentences.zh: 以文學聞於時。

translations.literal: He was famed in the age for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 元至正中，魯帥里中豪，集少壯保鄉曲。

translations.literal: In the middle of the Zhizheng period, Lu led the powerful men of his district, gathering young and strong to protect the township.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era he led local magnates and gathered young men to defend the township.

sentences.zh: 數具牛酒，為開陳順逆。
