translations.literal: Repeatedly he prepared oxen and wine and for them opened and explained obedience and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly feasted them and explained loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 眾皆遵約束，無敢為非義者。

translations.literal: The multitude all observed constraints; none dared do what was not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: All obeyed his rules; none dared commit wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 人號其里曰「君子鄉」。

translations.literal: People called his district "the District of Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: People called his neighborhood the District of Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，帝問丞相：「魯何官？

translations.literal: In the second month of year five the emperor asked the chief counselor: "What office does Lu hold?
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year the emperor asked the chief counselor what office Lu held.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「主事耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Only a section chief."
translations.idiomatic: The answer was, "Only a section chief."

sentences.zh: 即日超六階，拜中順大夫、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: That very day he was jumped six ranks and appointed Central Upright Grand Master and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Lu was promoted six ranks to central upright grand master and vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 魯以「順」字犯其父諱，辭，就朝請下階。

translations.literal: Lu, because the character shun in the title violated his father's taboo, declined and at court requested to descend one step on the stairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lu declined because the word shun in his title violated his father's taboo and asked to stand one step lower at court.

sentences.zh: 吏部持典制，不之許。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel held to canonical regulations and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel refused, citing regulations.

sentences.zh: 戍將捕獲倭人，帝命歸之。

translations.literal: Border garrison troops captured Japanese pirates; the emperor ordered them returned.
translations.idiomatic: When border troops captured Japanese raiders, the emperor ordered their return.

sentences.zh: 儒臣草詔，上閱魯稿大悅，曰：「頃陶凱文已起人意，魯復如此，文運其昌乎！」

translations.literal: Confucian ministers drafted the edict; the emperor on reading Lu's draft was greatly pleased and said: "Recently Tao Kai's writing already stirred men's minds; Lu is again like this—the literary fortune perhaps flourishes!"
translations.idiomatic: Confucian officials drafted the edict, but the emperor greatly preferred Lu's version, saying, "Tao Kai's prose already stirs the mind; Lu's does the same—the literary fortune is flourishing!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，命主京畿鄉試。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to preside over the metropolitan regional examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to supervise the capital regional examination.

sentences.zh: 甘露降鐘山，群臣以詩賦獻，帝獨褒魯。

translations.literal: Sweet dew fell on Bell Mountain; the hundred ministers presented poetry and fu; the emperor alone praised Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When sweet dew fell on Bell Mountain, ministers presented poems, but the emperor singled out Lu's for praise.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月引疾歸，道卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he cited illness and returned home; he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month he retired citing illness and died on the journey home.

sentences.zh: 淳安徐尊生嘗曰：「南京有博學士二人，以筆為舌者宋景濂，以舌為筆者曾得之也。」

translations.literal: Chun'an Xu Zunsheng once said: "At Nanjing there are two erudite scholars—Song Jinglian, whose brush is his tongue, and Zeng Dezhi, whose tongue is his brush."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zunsheng of Chun'an said, "Nanjing has two great scholars: Song Lian writes as he speaks, and Zeng Lu speaks as he writes."

sentences.zh: 魯屬文不留藁，其徒間有所輯錄，亦未成書雲。

translations.literal: Lu in composing texts left no drafts; his disciples occasionally compiled selections, yet also did not complete books.
translations.idiomatic: Lu kept no drafts; disciples compiled some of his work, but no complete book survived.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，禮部侍郎二十餘人，其知名者，自曾魯外，有劉崧、秦約、陳思道、張衡數人。

translations.literal: In Hongwu there were more than twenty Vice Ministers of Rites; among the renowned, apart from Zeng Lu, were Liu Song, Qin Yue, Chen Sidao, and Zhang Heng and several others.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty vice ministers of rites served in the Hongwu era; besides Lu, notable men included Liu Song, Qin Yue, Chen Sidao, and Zhang Heng.

sentences.zh: 崧自有傳。

translations.literal: Song has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 約，崇明人，字文仲。

translations.literal: Yue, a man of Chongming, style name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yue of Chongming was styled Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 博學，工辭章。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was erudite and skilled in belles lettres.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以文學舉。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu he was raised on account of literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he was recommended for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 召試《慎獨箴》，約文第一，立擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination on the Admonition on Solitary Vigilance, Yue's text ranked first and he was immediately promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On examination of his Admonition on Solitary Vigilance he ranked first and was immediately promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 母老乞歸。

translations.literal: His mother was old and he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 已，復召入陳三事，皆切直。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned in and presented three matters, all cutting and direct.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and presented three frank memorials.

sentences.zh: 仍乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: He still requested to return home and died.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to retire and died at home.

sentences.zh: 思道，山陰人，字執中。

translations.literal: Sidao, a man of Shanyin, style name Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sidao of Shanyin was styled Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 以進士授刑部主事。

translations.literal: As a jinshi he was appointed Section Chief of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: As a jinshi he became a section chief in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 帝賞其執法，超拜兵部侍郎，益勵風節，人莫敢幹以私。

translations.literal: The emperor prized his enforcement of law and jumped him to Vice Minister of War, further encouraging moral integrity—no one dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his strict enforcement of law and promoted him to vice minister of war; he upheld integrity so firmly that no one dared solicit favors.

sentences.zh: 改禮部，乞歸。

translations.literal: Changed to the Ministry of Rites; he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Rites, he then retired.

sentences.zh: 居家，不殖生產。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home, he did not accumulate productive property.
translations.idiomatic: At home he lived without amassing property.

sentences.zh: 守令造門不得見。

translations.literal: Magistrates and prefects coming to his gate could not obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials who called at his gate were refused audience.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 衡事別載。

translations.literal: Heng's affairs are recorded elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's career is recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 任昂，字伯顒，河陰人。

translations.literal: Ren Ang, style name Boyang, was a man of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Ang, styled Boyang, was from Heyin.

sentences.zh: 元末舉進士，除知寧晉縣，不赴。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Ningjin but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Ningjin but declined.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，薦起為襄垣訓導，擢御史。

translations.literal: In early Hongwu, on recommendation he was raised as Instructor of Xiangyuan and promoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Hongwu he was recommended as instructor at Xiangyuan and promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 十五年拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 帝加意太學，罷祭酒李敬、吳顒，命昂增定監規八條。

translations.literal: The emperor gave special attention to the National University, dismissed Chancellors Li Jing and Wu Yan, and ordered Ang to add and fix eight supervisory regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor focused on the National University, dismissed chancellors Li Jing and Wu Yan, and had Ang add eight supervisory regulations.

sentences.zh: 遂以曹國公李文忠、大學士宋訥兼領國子監事。

translations.literal: He thereupon had Duke of Cao Guo Li Wenzhong and Grand Academician Song Ne concurrently oversee National University affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong, duke of Cao, and Grand Academician Song Ne were then appointed to oversee the university.

sentences.zh: 會司諫關賢上言：「邇來郡邑所司非人，師道不立，歲選士多缺；

translations.literal: At the time Remonstrance Official Guan Xian memorialized: "Recently the officials in commanderies and districts are not the right men; the teacher's Way is not established, and each year selected scholars are mostly deficient;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Guan Xian reported that local officials were unfit, teaching had collapsed, and annual student selections fell short;

sentences.zh: 甚至俊秀生員，點充承差，乖朝廷育賢意。」

translations.literal: even outstanding student members are marked to fill courier posts—contrary to the court's intent to nurture worthies."
translations.idiomatic: even gifted students were assigned as couriers, contrary to the court's intent to nurture talent.

sentences.zh: 昂乃奏定天下：歲貢士從翰林院考試，以為殿最。

translations.literal: Ang thereupon memorialized fixing throughout the realm: annual tribute scholars should be examined by the Hanlin Academy to determine ranking.
translations.idiomatic: Ang memorialized that annual tribute students empire-wide should be examined by the Hanlin Academy for ranking.

sentences.zh: 明年，命科舉與薦舉並行。

translations.literal: The next year he ordered the examination system and recommendation to proceed in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: The next year civil examinations and recommendations were ordered to run in parallel.

sentences.zh: 昂條上科場成式，視前加詳，取士制始定。

translations.literal: Ang itemized the examination format in detail, more detailed than before—the system for selecting scholars was then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Ang detailed examination regulations more fully than before, fixing the selection system.

sentences.zh: 廣東都指揮狄崇、王臻以妾為繼室，乞封。

translations.literal: Guangdong Regional Commander Di Chong and Wang Zhen took concubines as successor wives and requested enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong commanders Di Chong and Wang Zhen asked to ennoble concubines promoted as successor wives.

sentences.zh: 下廷議，昂持不可，從之。

translations.literal: Sent down to court deliberation, Ang held it could not be done and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated; Ang objected and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂命昂及翰林院定嫡妾封贈例，因詔偕吏部定文官封贈例十一，廕敘例五，頒示中外。

translations.literal: He then ordered Ang and the Hanlin Academy to fix regulations for enfeoffing principal wives and concubines, and because of this edicted together with the Ministry of Personnel to fix eleven regulations for civil officials' enfeoffment and posthumous honors and five regulations for yin privilege, promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and the Hanlin Academy then codified enfeoffment rules for wives and concubines, and with the Ministry of Personnel issued eleven civil enfeoffment rules and five yin-succession rules for the empire.

sentences.zh: 尋請更定冕服之制。

translations.literal: Soon he requested further revision of the crown and robe system.
translations.idiomatic: He soon proposed revising court regalia.

sentences.zh: 及朝參坐次。

translations.literal: And seating order at court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He also set seating order at court audiences.

sentences.zh: 又奏毀天下淫祠，正祀典稱號：「蜀祀秦守李冰，附以漢守文翁、宋守張詠；

translations.literal: He also memorialized destroying licentious shrines throughout the realm and correcting canonical sacrifice titles: "In Shu they sacrifice to Qin Administrator Li Bing, with Han Administrator Wen Weng and Song Administrator Zhang Yong added;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized abolishing improper shrines and correcting canonical titles, listing approved local cults such as Li Bing in Shu with Wen Weng and Zhang Yong;

sentences.zh: 密縣祀太傅卓茂；

translations.literal: Mixi sacrifices Grand Tutor Zhuo Mao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Mao at Mixi;

sentences.zh: 鈞州祀丞相黃霸；

translations.literal: Junzhou sacrifices Chancellor Huang Ba;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ba at Junzhou;

sentences.zh: 彭澤祀丞相狄仁傑，皆遺愛在民。

translations.literal: Pengze sacrifices Chancellor Di Renjie—all left benevolence among the people.
translations.idiomatic: and Di Renjie at Pengze—all men whose benevolence endured among the people.

sentences.zh: 李龍遷祀於隆州，謝夷甫祀於福州，皆為民捍患。

translations.literal: Li Longqian was moved to sacrifice at Longzhou; Xie Yifu at Fuzhou—both defended the people against calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Longqian at Longzhou and Xie Yifu at Fuzhou had defended the people against disaster.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相陸遜以勞定國，宜祀於吳，以子抗、從子凱配。

translations.literal: Wu Chancellor Lu Xun through labor settled the state and should be sacrificed to in Wu, with his son Kang and nephew Kai as associates.
translations.idiomatic: Wu chancellor Lu Xun, who stabilized the state by his labors, should be worshipped in Wu with his son Kang and nephew Kai.

sentences.zh: 元總管李黼立祀江州，元帥余闕立廟安慶，皆以死勤事。

translations.literal: Yuan Administrator Li Fu established sacrifice at Jiangzhou; Yuan Marshal Yu Que established a temple at Anqing—both died diligent in service.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan officials Li Fu and Yu Que, who died in loyal service, were approved for sacrifice at Jiangzhou and Anqing.

sentences.zh: 從闕守皖，全家殉義者，有萬戶李宗可，宜配享闕廟。」

translations.literal: Following Que in guarding Wan, the whole family died in righteousness: Household Chief Li Zongke should receive associated sacrifice in Que's temple."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongke, who followed Yu Que and died with his household at Wan, was approved as an associate in Que's temple.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were replied acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 明年命以鄉飲酒禮頒天下，復令制大成樂器，分頒學宮。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to promulgate the district drinking ritual throughout the realm, and again ordered to make Great Completion ritual instruments and distribute them to schools.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he promulgated the district drinking rite empire-wide and had Great Completion instruments made for schools.

sentences.zh: 是時，以八事考課外吏，及次第雲南功賞，事不隸禮部，帝皆令昂主其議。

translations.literal: At the time, because of eight matters examining outer officials and the sequence of Yunnan merit rewards—affairs not subordinate to the Ministry of Rites—the emperor all ordered Ang to preside over their deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Though examining outer officials and Yunnan rewards lay outside ritual jurisdiction, the emperor had Ang deliberate them as well.

sentences.zh: 尋予告歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired.

sentences.zh: 李原名

translations.literal: Li Yuanming
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanming

sentences.zh: 李原名，字資善，安州人。

translations.literal: Li Yuanming, style name Zishan, was a man of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanming, styled Zishan, was from Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年，以通經儒士舉為御史。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year fifteen he was raised as a Confucian versed in the classics and made Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth Hongwu year he was recommended as a classicist and made censor.

sentences.zh: 二十年使平緬歸，言：「思倫發懷詐窺伺，宜嚴邊備。

translations.literal: In year twenty he was envoy to pacify Burma; on return he said: "Si Lunfa harbors deceit and watches for opportunity; border defense should be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in the twentieth year from a mission to pacify Burma, he warned that Si Lunfa was treacherous and border defenses must be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 靖江王以大理印行令旨，非法，為遠人所輕。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang used the Dali seal to issue command tokens—unlawful, and making light of the court before distant peoples."
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that the Prince of Jingjiang illegally issued orders with the Dali seal, inviting contempt from frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 稱旨，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Pleasing the intent, he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 自是遠方之事多咨之。

translations.literal: From this, affairs of distant regions were mostly consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter frontier affairs were often referred to him.

sentences.zh: 高麗奏遼東文、高、和、定州皆其國舊壤，乞就鐵嶺屯戍。

translations.literal: Goryeo memorialized that the eastern Liaodong prefectures Wen, Gao, He, and Ding were all its old territory and requested garrisoning at the Iron Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo claimed the Liaodong prefectures Wen, Gao, He, and Ding as its old lands and asked to garrison the Iron Ridge.

sentences.zh: 原名言：「數州皆入元版圖，屬於遼，高麗地以鴨綠江為界。

translations.literal: Yuanming said: "These several prefectures all entered the Yuan territorial map and belong to Liaodong; Goryeo's territory takes the Yalu River as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming replied that those prefectures had been under Yuan Liaodong administration and Goryeo's border was the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 今鐵嶺已置衛，不宜。」

translations.literal: Now the Iron Ridge already has a guard established—not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: A guard already stood at the Iron Ridge and the request should be denied.

sentences.zh: 復有陳請，帝命諭其國守分土，無生釁。

translations.literal: Again there was a petition; the emperor ordered instructing their state to keep to its territory and not create provocation.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo petitioned again, the emperor ordered it to keep within its borders.

sentences.zh: 安南歲貢方物，帝念其勞民，原名以帝意諭之，令三年一貢，自是為定制。

translations.literal: Annam each year presented tribute goods; the emperor, recalling the labor on the people, had Yuanming convey the imperial intent and instruct them, ordering tribute once every three years—from this it became the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying Annam's people, had Yuanming limit tribute to once every three years, which became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 又以帝命行養老之政，申明府州縣歲貢多寡之數，定官民巾服之式，皆著為令。

translations.literal: Also by imperial command he carried out the policy of caring for the aged, clarified the numbers for annual tribute from prefectures and counties, and fixed the forms of caps and robes for officials and commoners—all were written into ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He also implemented elderly-care policy, clarified tribute quotas, and codified dress regulations for officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 樂韶鳳

translations.literal: Yue Shaofeng
translations.idiomatic: Yue Shaofeng

sentences.zh: 樂韶鳳，字舜儀，全椒人。

translations.literal: Yue Shaofeng, style name Shunyi, was a man of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Shaofeng, styled Shunyi, was from Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 博學能文章。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and able in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was erudite and skilled in writing.

sentences.zh: 謁太祖於和陽，從渡江，參軍事。

translations.literal: He visited the Taizu emperor at Heyang, followed in crossing the Yangzi, and participated in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to the founding emperor at Heyang, followed him across the Yangzi, and served on military staff.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，授起居注，數遷。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year three he was appointed Daily Records Officer and repeatedly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Hongwu year he became a daily records officer and rose through several posts.

sentences.zh: 六年拜兵部尚書，與中書省、御史台、都督府定教練軍士法。

translations.literal: In year six he was appointed Minister of War and with the Secretariat, Censorate, and Military Commission fixed the regulations for drilling soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became minister of war and, with the secretariat, censorate, and military commission, set drill regulations.

sentences.zh: 改侍講學士，與承旨詹同正釋奠先師樂章，編集《大明日曆》。

translations.literal: Changed to Reader-in-Waiting; with Expositor Zhan Tong he corrected the music for sacrifice to the first teacher and compiled the Great Ming Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He became reader-in-waiting, corrected Confucian sacrifice music with Zhan Tong, and helped compile the Great Ming Calendar.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝以祭禮駕還，應用樂舞前導，命韶鳳等撰詞。

translations.literal: In year seven, when the emperor because of sacrifice rites returned from the imperial progress, music and dance should precede as guide—he ordered Shaofeng and others to compose the words.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the emperor returned from sacrifice, he ordered Shaofeng to compose lyrics for the procession music.

sentences.zh: 因撰《神降祥》、《神貺惠》、《酣酒》、《色荒》、《禽荒》諸曲以進，凡三十九章，曰《回鑾樂歌》，皆寓規諫。

translations.literal: He thereupon composed Spirit Descends in Auspice, Spirit Bestows Favor, Drunken with Wine, Lust for Color, Lust for Birds and Beasts and other pieces to present—altogether thirty-nine sections, entitled Music of the Returning Imperial Progress—all containing admonition within.
translations.idiomatic: He composed thirty-nine songs including Spirit Descends in Auspice and Lust for Color, entitled Music of the Returning Imperial Progress, each embedding remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 禮部具《樂舞圖》以上，命太常肄習之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites prepared the Music and Dance Diagram and presented it upward; the emperor ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to practice it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites submitted dance diagrams and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices rehearsed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝以舊韻出江左，多失正，命與廷臣參考中原雅音正之。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor, because the old rhymes came from the southeast and mostly missed correctness, ordered him with court ministers to consult central plains elegant sounds and correct them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, finding southeastern rhymes inaccurate, the emperor ordered him and court scholars to revise them against central plains pronunciation.

sentences.zh: 書成，名《洪武正韻》。

translations.literal: When the book was completed it was named Correct Rhymes of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The resulting work was titled Correct Rhymes of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 又命孝陵寢朔望祭祀及登壇脫舄諸禮議，皆詳稽故實。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to deliberate the new and full moon sacrifices at the Xiaoling mausoleum and the rites of mounting the altar and removing shoes—all detailed in examining past facts.
translations.idiomatic: He also researched Xiaoling mausoleum sacrifices and altar protocols in detail.

sentences.zh: 俱從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋病免。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復起為祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long he was again raised as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 奉詔定皇太子與諸王往復書答刂禮，考據精詳，屢被褒答。

translations.literal: By imperial command he fixed the etiquette of letters exchanged between the heir apparent and the various princes; his textual verification was precise and detailed, and he was repeatedly praised in reply.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he codified correspondence etiquette between the heir apparent and princes; his research was meticulous and won repeated praise.

sentences.zh: 十三年致仕歸，以壽終。

translations.literal: In year thirteen he retired and returned home; he ended his life through longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he retired and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 弟暉、禮、毅，皆知名。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Hui, Li, and Yi were all renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Hui, Li, and Yi were also well known.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明初之議禮也，宋濂方家居，諸儀率多陶安裁定。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: In the early Ming deliberation on ritual, Song Lian was still at home; the various ceremonies were mostly drawn up and settled by Tao An.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: When the Ming first debated ritual, Song Lian was still in retirement and Tao An settled most of the forms.

sentences.zh: 大祀禮專用安議，其餘參匯諸說，從其所長：祫禘用詹同，時享用硃升，釋奠、耕耤用錢用壬，五祀用崔亮，朝會用劉基，祝祭用魏觀，軍禮用陶凱。

translations.literal: Great-sacrifice ritual exclusively used An's deliberations; the rest combined various opinions, following each man's strength: collective and seasonal sacrifice used Zhan Tong, seasonal offerings used Zhu Sheng, Confucian sacrifice and royal plowing used Qian Yongren, the five sacrifices used Cui Liang, court audiences used Liu Ji, prayer-sacrifice used Wei Guan, military ritual used Tao Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices followed An exclusively; other rites combined specialists—Zhan Tong for collective and seasonal rites, Zhu Sheng for seasonal offerings, Qian Yongren for Confucian sacrifice and plowing, Cui Liang for the five sacrifices, Liu Ji for court audiences, Wei Guan for prayer sacrifices, and Tao Kai for military ritual.

sentences.zh: 皆能援據經義，酌古準今，郁然成一代休明之治。

translations.literal: All were able to cite classical meaning, weigh antiquity against the present, and richly form the brilliant governance of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: All cited the classics, weighed antiquity against the present, and helped shape a brilliant age of governance.

sentences.zh: 雖折中斷制，裁自上心，諸臣之功亦曷可少哉。

translations.literal: Although the final compromise and judgment and cutting were from the ruler's own mind, how could the merit of the various ministers be slighted?
translations.idiomatic: Though final decisions rested with the emperor, the ministers' contributions can hardly be slighted.
